title: Vanishing and Uniqueness of Quantum Diffusion Solutions
exact_target: Decide whether nontrivial sixth-order quantum diffusion solutions can contain vacuum points, and whether its weak solutions are unique.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 30001641 (OWR-4536-002). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.
Classical and Quantum Mechanical Models of Many-Particle Systems (2010), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2010/54, pp. 3159--3236; official report source and mathematical context.
Official EMS Press PDF of the same Oberwolfach report; PDF pages 37--38, printed pages 3195--3196.
sixth-order quantum equation; reference in the saved dated catalogue literature review.

status_qualification: A zero-mass solution would make the vacuum-existence question trivial, so the intended physical question concerns nonzero density. The weak class and meaning of a vacuum point must be fixed before asking either existence or uniqueness. The source proves nonnegative weak existence but does not infer either of these two answers.
